header.running_head: The Du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ Recited when Sighting the New Moon and when Noticing Thunder, Clouds or Wind

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ هٰذَا الشَّهْرِ وَخَيْرِ الْقَدَرِ وَأَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهٖ
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the new moon, he would remark, "The moon of good and virtue." He would then recite the following du'aa thrice:
"O Allaah! I ask You for the good of this month and for the best of destinies and I seek Your protection from its evil"[^2]
The Du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ Recited when he Noticed Thunder, Clouds and Wind

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ لَا تَقْتُلْنَا بِغَضَبِكَ وَلَا تُهْلِكْنَا بِعَذَابِكَ وَعَافِنَا قَبْلَ ذٰلِكَ
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard thunderclaps, he recited:
"O Allaah! Let not Your wrath kill us, let not Your punishment destroy us but rather grant us safety before that"[^3]

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا وَخَيْرَ مَا فِيْهَا وَخَيْرَ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهٖ وَأَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا فِيْهَا وَشَرِّ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهٖ
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that whenever the wind blew violently, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say:
"O Allaah! I ask You for its good, the good in it and the good it has been sent for. I also seek Your protection from its evil, the evil in it and the evil (punishment) it has been sent for"[^4]

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed a cloud forming on the horizon, he would leave what he was doing. In fact, if he was performing salaah, he would shorten it. He would then recite the du'aa:
"O Allaah! I seek Your protection from its evil"
If rain then fell, he would say: (اَللّٰهُمَّ صَيِّبًا هَنِيْئًا)
"O Allaah! Make this a pleasant downpour"[^5]

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ إِنَّا نَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أُرْسِلَ بِهٖ
blocks.text:
